description: The plot illustrates the relationship between co-occurrence number and accuracy (ACC) for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10 to 1000 with tick labels at 10, 100, and 1000. The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” and uses a linear scale, ranging from 60 to 80 with tick labels at 60, 65, 70, 75, and 80. The “Base” method is represented by a black line with circular markers, starting at approximately 60% at a co-occurrence number of 10 and increasing to approximately 65% at a co-occurrence number of 1000. The “FT” method is represented by a blue line with triangular markers, beginning at approximately 63% at a co-occurrence number of 10 and rising to approximately 73% at a co-occurrence number of 1000. The “IKE” method is shown as a red line with triangular markers, starting at approximately 65% at a co-occurrence number of 10 and reaching approximately 70% at a co-occurrence number of 1000. The “MEND” method is represented by a brown line with diamond markers, starting at approximately 67% at a co-occurrence number of 10 and increasing to approximately 73% at a co-occurrence number of 1000. The “MEMIT” method is shown as a purple line with square markers, beginning at approximately 68% at a co-occurrence number of 10 and rising to approximately 74% at a co-occurrence number of 1000. Finally, the “ROME” method is represented by a green line with square markers, starting at approximately 74% at a co-occurrence number of 10 and increasing to approximately 85% at a co-occurrence number of 1000.
caption_used: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) performance of six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME) on Llama2 across varying co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis represents 'Co-occurrence Number' on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10^1 to 10^3, while the y-axis shows 'ACC (%)' on a linear scale from 60% to 80%. ROME consistently outperforms all other methods, achieving an accuracy of approximately 85% at the highest co-occurrence number. MEMIT and MEND exhibit similar trends, with MEMIT slightly surpassing MEND at lower co-occurrence numbers but falling behind at higher values. FT demonstrates the steepest growth rate, increasing by nearly 10% across the range, while Base remains relatively stable, showing minimal improvement. IKE starts with the highest initial accuracy but stabilizes at around 70%, falling behind MEMIT and MEND at higher co-occurrence numbers.
